title: How do you guys generate your game sprites?
author: hugomcjohnson
selftext: I've been using chatgpt to generate my game sprites for a darkest dungeon style combat system where I need one static sprite per character ability/effect, but I'm getting more and more annoyed at how hard it is to keep the characters consistent between the sprites. No matter my instructions it keeps changing the scale and proprtions of characters and adds weird moiré to textures. I'm wondering if there's any good alternatives out there for something that isn't pixel art and you can use to make consistent characters in different positions?

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body: You can try research some dedicated art models in comfyui and training loras and it'll get you as close as you can get atm. But consistency is Ai's fundamental flaw atm.

comments.author: AliAlHamwi
comments.body:
The drift is structural. Each generation is a fresh roll, and the prompt is
    the only thing carrying your character between them, so anything you did not
    spell out gets re-decided. Proportions and scale are exactly the things
    nobody spells out.
    
    What fixes it is giving the model the character as an image rather than as a
    description, on every generation. Ludo.ai has a reference mode that locks the
    style and the subject together, so the same character comes back across
    separate generations instead of being redesigned each time. I work on it, so
    discount accordingly, and there are 30 free credits at signup if you want to
    throw your roster at it: https://ludo.ai
    
    The moiré is a separate bug and worth fixing on its own. It shows up when a
    high-frequency texture gets resampled down to your sprite size. Generate the
    texture detail coarser than feels right, or render bigger and downscale in
    one step rather than letting the model draw fine weave at final size.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
For chat gpt, you have almost no control. You need either to reroll million times, or to send it a reference sheet with every prompt

If you wanna more control, get yourself Krita and plugin Krita AI Diffusion. That way you could draw the scribbles and make AI to heavily rely on them when generating. It will keep all the shapes and proportions. You can also use your GPT concepts for control nets

If you have weak GPU, you could find a hardware for rent and put ComfyUI in a cloud
